import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset from the specified path
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv', low_memory=False)
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset not found. Please ensure 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' exists.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Filter for a recent and relevant time period to show clear trends (e.g., 2015 onwards)
df_recent = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] >= 2015].copy()

# Clean up breed names: strip whitespace and handle potential inconsistencies
df_recent['Rasse1Text'] = df_recent['Rasse1Text'].str.strip()

# Identify the top 10 most common breeds in this period.
# This gives a stable view of the most significant breeds over the last several years.
top_10_breeds = df_recent['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataframe to include only data for these top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df_recent[df_recent['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)]

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count for each of the top breeds
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='Count')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots for a professional look
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create the figure and axes with an appropriate size for a detailed line chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 12))

# Create the line plot using seaborn, which handles the grouping by 'hue' automatically
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='Count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    ax=ax,
    palette='tab10',  # A distinct and colorblind-friendly palette
    linewidth=3,
    marker='o',
    markersize=8,
    legend='full'
)

# --- Customization and Labels for Clarity ---

# Set a clear and descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title('Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich (2015-Present)', fontsize=24, weight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=18, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=18, labelpad=15)

# Customize tick parameters for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=14, rotation=45)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=14)

# Ensure the x-axis ticks are integers, as they represent years
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
ax.grid(which='major', linestyle='--', linewidth='0.5')

# Improve the legend by moving it outside the plot area to prevent overlap
# and giving it a title
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=14,
    title_fontsize=16
)

# Add a subtle background color to the plot area
ax.set_facecolor('#f5f5f5')

# Add a text annotation for context
latest_year = df_recent['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
ax.text(0.99, 0.01, f'Data Source: City of Zurich, Open Data | Latest Data: {latest_year}',
        transform=ax.transAxes,
        fontsize=12,
        color='gray',
        ha='right',
        va='bottom')

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the final figure as a high-quality PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
